To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the affective content analysis of video is possible and that it is a very promising tool for the development of personalized TV systems.

(1) the affective content is a valuable and important information source for the future personalized TV systems; (2) the content of an affective video signal can be effectively represented by the low-level audiovisual features, such as the pitch and the energy of the soundtrack, or the brightness and the colorfulness of the video; and (3) the affective labels can be predicted from the content features by using a machine learning technique, such as the support vector machines.
the affective video analysis is an interesting research field with many potential applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two questions: (1) What can we do to extract affective content from a video clip? (2) How can we use the information about the affective content for personalizing the TV experience?
extracting the information about the affective content from video.
the following questions: How can we represent and model the affective content? What are the possibilities to extract this content from a video signal? What are the applications of this content?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the affective content analysis of video is a very challenging research problem with many open issues.
the affective content is a promising and important research topic that can be applied for improving the quality of the personalized TV services.
affective content analysis has a high potential to improve the content recommendation functionality of future PVRs or VOD systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to show how the affective content analysis of audio and video can be used in a number of applications, such as the affective search of video, affective content recommendation, affective content summarization, affective content browsing, affective content adaptation, affective content personalization, and affective content annotation.
we have developed a system that can automatically analyze the affective content in a video and then use the extracted information to provide personalized recommendations to the user.
we have developed a novel framework for the automatic analysis of affective content in video, based on a combination of audio and visual features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the affective content analysis of video can be used for enhancing the content-based video retrieval and recommendation functionalities of the next generation PVRs and video on demand services.
we can now analyze the affective content and affective labels of video signals and, in particular, of TV programs, in a reliable and efficient way.
the affective content analysis of audiovisual signals can provide a powerful means to personalize the content selection and recommendation processes.
